in_text_mentions: the right groin area, refractory to analgesics. Further evaluation by CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast revealed a wedge-shaped area of hypoenhancement with abrupt occlusion of the posterior segmental artery, along with a positive cortical rim sign. panels.rationale: DMSA renal scintigraphy from a patient with renal infarction shows a small left kidney with reduced tracer uptake and reduced relative function, consistent with residual infarcted renal parenchyma. Nuclear scintigraphy is represented as 'other' modality because no specific nuclear medicine option is available.

panels.figure_caption: DMSA static renal scintigraphy at 30 days from discharge shows a small left kidney with reduced uptake of the tracer.
in_text_mentions: To exclude a paraneoplastic syndrome, a PET-CT with FDG was performed, which did not show areas of focal/pathological uptake of the tracer. Oncological markers, such as AFP, CEA, CA 19-9, PSA, beta-HCG, aldosterone, and 24-h urinary metanephrines, were in the normal range (Table 2). Moreover, we performed sequential multimodal imaging studies during hospitalization (Figure 2, Figure 3 and Figure 4).

After 30 days, a follow-up CT scan showed resolution of the renal artery thrombus with improved vascularization of the left kidney, and persistence of residual infarcted areas (Figure 2D–H). DMSA static renal scintigraphy showed a small left kidney with an estimated residual relative renal function of 28% (Figure 4).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial DWI MRI of a human patient with arrows pointing to the right kidney infarct (no restricted diffusion, useful negative finding); article title explicitly attributes the case to renal infarction. B: Axial T2-weighted MRI of a human patient showing hypointense signal in the infarcted right kidney (arrows); the case is a documented renal infarction. C: Post-contrast T1 MRI of a human patient demonstrating classic wedge-shaped non-enhancing infarcted areas with preserved capsular (cortical rim) enhancement in the right kidney; article title and caption directly attribute findings to renal infarction.
